TRS-80 Level II subset

Two significant name characters, historical keyword recognition and separate typed namespaces. DEFINT A-Z selects signed integers by initial letter; DEFSNG, DEFDBL and DEFSTR select other defaults. Explicit %, !, # or $ suffixes override defaults. Integer assignment/CINT floors then checks -32768…32767; FIX truncates toward zero. Single/double values remain host doubles, not MBF values.

Implicit THEN, nested IF and subroutine-local FOR stack cleanup are implemented. RETURN discards unfinished loops created within that call; NEXT cannot consume a caller’s loop. Arrays, DATA and READ honor destination types. RND with positive integer n draws 1…n; zero draws a fresh fraction. Negative reseeding and fractional bounds are not verified historical behavior.

INPUT uppercases, can collect missing fields over several prompts, retains remaining values on blank input and reports ignored extra fields. CLEAR resets values/arrays/functions/stacks/DATA cursor and records a bounded string-space request, but does not emulate a physical string heap.

CLS appends a screen-clear marker. PRINT @ validates 0…1023 and supplies column indentation; it does not overwrite prior rows. POS uses a logical 64-column position independently of the 40/80-column browser display. PRINT zones are 16 columns. MEM produces a diagnostic; POKE is unsupported. ROM glyphs, exact control characters, tape encoding and memory checksums are not emulated.

Typed cassette records and sequential OPEN/CLOSE are described in the device chapter. OPEN/CLOSE are an explicit disk-style extension alongside the cassette interface, not a claim of cassette-only Level II syntax. Try Virtual notebook. Historical physical multiline records require an explicitly documented compatibility transcription, never automatic rewriting.
